summary: Walther Prellwitz worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg (~1881–1885) studying under Adalbert Bezzenberger, later serving there as Privatdozent (1901) and ao. Professor of Comparative Linguistics (1924).

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at Munich, Strasbourg (Ph.D. under Ernst Leumann, ~1900–1904), and Berlin (Habilitation, ~1914–1917). He held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (1905–1920) and the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (1920–1923). He held Munich posts including Privatdozent (1926, 1932) and Dean (1935–1945), led a department at Ahnenerbe (1936), and served as president of Deutsche Akademie (1943).

Wanda Dynowska was active in religious studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Lausanne, served as general secretary of the Polish Theosophical Society (1921), and founded the Indo-Polish Library in 1944.
Wang Pachow worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He was a student of Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang works in Buddhist studies and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Cambridge, consulted for the Classical Art Research Centre (2017–2020), lectured at Thammasat University (2019), and served as Project Assistant at Oxford (attested 2019–2022).

Linguist and Indologist Warren Crawford Cowgill studied at Stanford (B.A. ~1948–1952 under Hermann Fränkel) and Yale (Ph.D. ~1952–1957 under Paul Tedesco and Paul Thieme). He served as Assistant Professor at Yale University from 1956 to 1972.

Warren Lee Todd works in philosophy and Indology. He completed his PhD at Lancaster University under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, having also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and traditional teacher Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007), where his MA supervisors were Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, alongside teachers Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Waso Harada, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University (MA 1984). He held posts at Koyasan University (1992), Ryukoku University (1999–2006), and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2002–2007).
Watari Yanai was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1900 to 1903 and held a post there from ~1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1951). He held positions at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1968–1974) and the University of Tokyo (~1974–1989), working in philosophy and other fields.

Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He pursued his doctoral studies as a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under supervisor Mark Rowe (attested 2026).

Wayne Proudfoot is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned a Master of Theology (~1965–1969) and PhD (~1969–1972) at Harvard. He taught at Fordham University (~1969–1972) and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2018).

Wei Lin, a scholar of sinology and archaeology, studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State (Ph.D. under John C. Huntington). He held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum and Transylvania University (attested 2007).
Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. He serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University (attested 2026).

Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, when he joined the faculty at the University of Chicago.

Wei-jen Teng studied at Chicago and earned a PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. He has taught at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and serves as Professor and Dean at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Wei-ming Tu studied at Tunghai University (B.A.) and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1962–1968). He held posts at Princeton (1968–1971), UC Berkeley (1971–1981), the East-West Center (1990–1991), Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008), and Harvard University (1999–2010).
